name: email-permitted-localpart-case-shift-san-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees rfc822Name is the full mailbox 'Foo@example.com' (capital F on the local-part). The leaf's SAN rfc822Name is 'foo@example.com' (lowercase). RFC 5280 §7.5 requires the local-parts of two rfc822Names to be an exact match for the names to be considered equal; 'Foo' and 'foo' differ, so the leaf's SAN does not match the constraint, the leaf is outside the permitted subtree, and the chain must be rejected. A validator that case-folds the local-part during comparison (e.g. applying pkcs9CaseIgnoreMatch despite the constraint being an rfc822Name) will incorrectly accept.
references: RFC 2985 5.4 (PKCS#9 directory attribute matching rule — not invoked by RFC 5280 for constraint matching)
notes: Permit-direction companion to email-excluded-localpart-case-shift-dn-attr-valid-rfc5280. Same §7.5 exact-local-part rule, opposite consequence: in the permit direction a case mismatch means the leaf falls outside the subtree and must be rejected (here, expected: invalid). A validator that compares local-parts case-insensitively will be inconsistent — applying its non-RFC rule lets through a leaf the spec rejects.

Routed through the SAN rather than the DN emailAddress attribute to isolate the local-part comparison rule from the orthogonal question of whether the DN-fallback path is enforced at all (Go/Rust/pyca silently no-op that fallback, which would mask this test if it lived on the DN side).
